blocks.title: jfr print

blocks.text: For a graphical view, open the file in JDK Mission Control (a separate download, no longer bundled with the JDK) or in IntelliJ IDEA. Its flame graph and "Memory" and "Lock instances" pages are built on exactly these events. Events worth knowing by name: `jdk.ExecutionSample` (CPU sampling), `jdk.JavaMonitorEnter` (lock contention), `jdk.GarbageCollection`, `jdk.ObjectAllocationSample`, `jdk.OldObjectSample` (candidate leaks, with optional reference chains), `jdk.FileRead`, `jdk.SocketRead`, `jdk.CPULoad`.

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: JFR's sampler records Java threads at a safe-ish moment roughly every 10 or 20 ms (the exact period depends on the setting). It is a statistical profile: good for finding the top few hot methods, not for timing one particular call.

### GUI tools and the remote story

`jconsole` and VisualVM (a separate download) connect to a JVM, locally or over JMX, and show live graphs of heap, threads, classes and CPU, let you invoke a thread dump or heap dump with a button, and browse MBeans. They are good for exploring a development or staging process. For remote production processes, the common pattern is different: expose metrics through Micrometer or the platform MXBeans to Prometheus and Grafana, and keep the command-line tools for the moment you are on the box (or in the container, via `kubectl exec`).

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Do not open JMX remote access (`-Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.port=...`) without authentication and TLS. An open JMX port is remote code execution for anyone who can reach it. The local attach used by `jcmd` and `jstack` requires the same operating-system user as the target process, which is why `jcmd` says "Permission denied" if you run it as a different user from the application.

blocks.title: Real world
blocks.text: In containers the JVM's pid is often 1 and the image may have only a JRE-like runtime without the tools. Either use a JDK-based image (so `jcmd` exists), or add JFR flags to the startup command and copy the `.jfr` out afterwards. Spring Boot Actuator exposes `/actuator/threaddump` and `/actuator/heapdump` for the same purposes; restrict those endpoints, they leak internals.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: How would you find out why a Java process is using 100% CPU? Find the hot thread: `top -H -p <pid>` shows per-thread CPU. Match that thread id to the `nid` in a `jstack` dump (converting to hex if your JDK prints it that way), then read its stack. Take several dumps to confirm it is always in the same place, or record a JFR and look at the hot-methods view. Check GC activity with `jstat -gcutil` as well, since GC threads can be the cause.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
The JDK diagnostic tools attach to a running JVM; start with `jcmd <pid> help`, `Thread.print`, `GC.heap_info` and `JFR.start`.

- A thread dump shows what every thread is doing now; three dumps a few seconds apart show who is stuck; deadlocks are reported automatically.
- `jstat -gcutil` plus `jmap -histo:live` tell you whether memory is leaking and which class is piling up; a heap dump with a dominator tree and GC-root path tells you who holds it.
- JFR is a low-overhead, always-available recorder; read it with `jfr summary`, `jfr view` and `jfr print`, or with Mission Control.
- Heap dumps and JMX ports are security-sensitive: protect both, and arm `HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError` before you need it.
#### Reflection and Annotations

items.question: Which call returns a private method declared in the class itself: `getMethod` or `getDeclaredMethod`? Which one also finds inherited public methods?
items.answer: `getDeclaredMethod` finds a private method of that class. `getMethod` finds public methods only, but includes inherited ones.

items.question: What does this print? `Method m = String.class.getMethod("length");` `System.out.println(m.invoke("hello"));`
items.answer: It prints `5`: the result is boxed to `Integer`, printed by `println(Object)`.

items.question: A method called through `Method.invoke` throws `IllegalStateException`. What exception does the caller of `invoke` see, and how do you get the original?
items.answer: An `InvocationTargetException`; call `getCause()` to get the `IllegalStateException`.

items.question: Your custom annotation is never found by `field.getAnnotation(...)` although it is clearly present in the source. What is the most likely cause?
items.answer: The annotation lacks `@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)`. The default is `CLASS`, which is not visible to reflection.

items.question: After moving to a newer JDK a library fails with `InaccessibleObjectException`. Name two ways to deal with it.
items.answer: Upgrade the library to a version that does not reflect into JDK internals, or add `--add-opens` `module/package=ALL-UNNAMED` as a temporary workaround.

items.question: Why do build-time annotation processors give faster start-up than reflection-based scanning?
items.answer: The metadata is processed and code generated during compilation, so at start-up there is nothing to scan or look up reflectively.

blocks.text: #### Dynamic Proxies and Method Handles

items.question: Can `Proxy.newProxyInstance` create a proxy of the concrete class `ArrayList`? Why or why not?
items.answer: No. JDK proxies can only implement interfaces; for classes you need a subclass-generating library such as CGLIB or ByteBuddy.

items.question: In a Spring bean, method `a()` calls `this.b()`, and `b()` is annotated `@Transactional`. Is a transaction started for `b()`? Why?
items.answer: No. The call is made on `this`, the raw target, so it bypasses the proxy that applies the transaction advice.

items.question: What does this do? `MethodHandle h = lookup.findVirtual(String.class, "length",` `MethodType.methodType(int.class)); Object o = h.invokeExact("abc");`
items.answer: It throws `WrongMethodTypeException` at run time: the call site's type is `(String)Object` but the handle is `(String)int`. Cast the result: `int n = (int) h.invokeExact("abc");`.

items.question: Which exception type should a proxy handler rethrow after `method.invoke(target, args)` fails with `InvocationTargetException`?
items.answer: The cause (`e.getCause()`), so the caller sees the original business exception instead of a reflection wrapper.

items.question: Name the VarHandle operation that atomically changes a value only if it still equals an expected one.
items.answer: `compareAndSet(...)` (or `weakCompareAndSet`, `compareAndExchange`).

blocks.text: #### Class Loaders and ServiceLoader

items.question: What does `String.class.getClassLoader()` return, and why?
items.answer: `null`: the bootstrap loader is implemented in native code and has no `ClassLoader` object.

items.question: Two class loaders each load class `Plugin` from the same `.class` file. Is `c1 == c2`? Can an instance of one be assigned to a variable of the other's type?
items.answer: `c1 != c2`. The instance cannot be assigned or cast; the result is a `ClassCastException` saying class `Plugin` cannot be cast to class `Plugin`.

items.question: What is wrong here? The class `Config` has `static final Map<String, Object> CACHE`, is loaded by a web-app loader, and a daemon thread started by a library inside that app keeps running after undeploy.
items.answer: The running thread references the loader (through its classes), so the loader and all its classes, including `Config.CACHE`, can never be unloaded: a Metaspace leak on every redeploy. Stop threads on undeploy.

items.question: Where does a provider jar declare its implementation of `com.example.spi.Greeter` on the class path?
items.answer: In a resource file `META-INF/services/com.example.spi.Greeter` listing the fully qualified class names, one per line.

items.question: Why does `defineClass` for a name starting with `java.` fail even in a custom loader?
items.answer: The JVM prohibits user-defined loaders from defining classes in `java.*` packages (`SecurityException:` `Prohibited package name: java.lang`); core classes must come from the bootstrap loader.

blocks.text: #### The Module System (JPMS)

items.question: Which module is required by every module without being declared?
items.answer: `java.base`.

items.question: A class is `public` but lives in a package the module does not export. Who can use it?
items.answer: Only code inside the same module. Other modules cannot compile against it, and reflection into it is also refused.

items.question: What is the difference between `requires` and `requires transitive`?
items.answer: With `requires transitive m`, any module that requires mine automatically reads `m` too. Use it when `m`'s types appear in your public signatures.

items.question: What is a split package, and what does the module system do about it?
items.answer: The same package name exported by two different modules. The module system refuses to start (or compile) such a configuration to avoid ambiguity.

items.question: What does this print when run on the class path (no `module-info`): `System.out.println(Main.class.getModule().isNamed());`?
items.answer: `false`: class-path code is in the unnamed module.

items.question: Why can a `jlink` image be much smaller than a JDK installation?
items.answer: It contains only the modules your application (transitively) requires, found with `jdeps`, instead of all ~70 JDK modules (69 on this JDK 21 build).

blocks.text: #### Calling Native Code: JNI and the Foreign Function and Memory API

items.question: Name two reasons a JNI bug is more dangerous than a Java bug.
items.answer: A native error can crash the entire JVM (segmentation fault) instead of throwing an exception, and native code is unchecked: no bounds checking, no garbage collection, manual memory management.

items.question: In which Java version did the FFM API become final, and what was it before?
items.answer: Java 22 (JEP 454). Before that it was a preview API in Java 19 to 21 and an incubator API in 14 to 18.

items.question: What does this do after the `try` block ends? `MemorySegment s; try (Arena a = Arena.ofConfined()) { s =` `a.allocate(8); } s.get(ValueLayout.JAVA_BYTE, 0);`
items.answer: It throws `IllegalStateException` ("Already closed"): the arena freed the memory and the segment is no longer accessible.

items.question: Which class holds the C function signature, and which finds a function by name?
items.answer: `FunctionDescriptor` describes the signature; `SymbolLookup` (for example `linker.defaultLookup()`) finds the symbol.

items.question: What does a `ValueLayout.ADDRESS` parameter in a `FunctionDescriptor` correspond to in C?
items.answer: A pointer (`void *`, `char *`, `struct *`).

blocks.text: #### Troubleshooting Playbook

items.question: A Java process shows `%CPU` near 100 for a single thread in `top -H` with id 2952. How do you find the Java code responsible? What can differ between JDK builds?
items.answer: Search the `jstack` dump for `nid=2952` and read that thread's stack, or use a JFR hot-methods view. Many JDK builds print `nid` in hex, so if the decimal search finds nothing, search for `nid=0xb88` (`printf '%x' 2952`).

items.question: What does this thread-dump excerpt tell you? Three dumps in a row show `"http-nio-8080-exec-1"` through `-exec-200` all `WAITING` in `HikariPool.getConnection`, and CPU is 3%.
items.answer: The database connection pool is exhausted: all request threads wait for a connection while nobody computes. Look for threads holding connections (leaked or stuck on a slow call) and fix timeouts and resource closing.

items.question: Why is raising `-Xmx` not a fix for a leak?
items.answer: A leak grows without bound, so a bigger heap only delays the failure and makes the dump bigger. Fix what holds the objects.

items.question: `OutOfMemoryError: unable to create native thread` appears while `jstat` shows the heap is only 40% used. Name two possible causes.
items.answer: The OS or container refused another thread (process or pid limit), or there is not enough native memory left for thread stacks. Too many threads is the underlying cause, usually an unbounded executor or a thread-per-task loop.

items.question: What is wrong with taking `jmap -histo:live` every second on a busy production server?
items.answer: `:live` forces a full collection every time, pausing the application and adding GC load. Sample rarely, and prefer a recording or a single dump.

items.question: The JVM was killed with exit code 137 in a container and there was no Java stack trace. Which memory is not covered by `-Xmx`, and which tool shows it?
items.answer: Exit code 137 means the process received SIGKILL, typically from the out-of-memory killer. Metaspace, thread stacks, the code cache and direct buffers are outside the heap. Native Memory Tracking (`-XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary` plus `jcmd <pid> VM.native_memory`) breaks them down.

blocks.text: #### The Diagnostics Toolbox

items.question: Which tool gives you a thread dump, and which line at the end of the dump tells you about a deadlock?
items.answer: `jstack <pid>` or `jcmd <pid> Thread.print`. If a cycle of monitors exists, the dump ends with "Found one Java-level deadlock", followed by who holds and who waits for each lock.

items.question: In `jstat -gcutil` output, the `O` column climbs after every collection and `FGC` keeps increasing. What does it suggest, and what do you take next?
items.answer: Objects are surviving every collection and the old generation fills: a probable leak or an undersized heap. Take a `jmap -histo:live` to see which class grows, then a heap dump and look at the dominator tree and path to GC roots.

items.question: Why does `jmap -histo:live` pause the application, and what does `[B` mean in its output?
items.answer: `:live` triggers a full collection first, which stops the application threads. `[B` is the internal name of `byte[]`.

items.question: What is wrong with this startup line for a production service? `java -Dcom.sun.management.jmxremote.port=9010` `-jar app.jar`
items.answer: The JMX port is open with no authentication and no TLS (these are off by default when only the port property is set), so anyone who can reach port 9010 can control the JVM. Add `authenticate=true`, `ssl=true` or bind it to localhost and tunnel.

items.question: You need a profile of a service that is already running and was started without any JFR flags. Give the command.
items.answer: `jcmd <pid> JFR.start name=live settings=profile duration=60s filename=/tmp/live.jfr`, then read it with `jfr view hot-methods /tmp/live.jfr` or Mission Control.

items.question: A heap dump shows 2 GB retained by one `HashMap` held in a static field. Which view in MAT finds this, and what do you do with the answer?
items.answer: The dominator tree (sorted by retained size) finds it; "path to GC roots" shows the static field. The fix is to bound or evict the map (size limit, TTL, a cache library) or to stop adding to it.
